A well detailed case study is conducted to monitor the electricity consumption in the real time environment, and the proposed scheduling strategy is simulated to validate the performance of algorithm. Evaluation of experimental results demonstrated that multi-objective SFO algorithm obtains significant electricity cost reduction and maximizes resource utilization when compared to other most popular algorithms, such as, First Fit, Best Fit, Firefly algorithm (FA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Invasive Weed Optimization (IWO).

articleTitle: An Optimal Speech Recognition Module for Patient's Voice Monitoring System in Smart Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 Renewable Energies, Power Systems & Green Inclusive Economy (REPS-GIE)
abstract: During recent years, health care domain has rapidly developed in which patients and medical resources are directly connected with the smart way that enables Smart Health Care. The growth in design and development of a speech automated system will provide a life assistant service in smart health care environment. In automating the speech system, speech recognition is one of the basic steps to understand the human recognition and their behaviors. These speech recognition systems will be very much accessible for speakers who suffer from dysarthria, a neurological disability that damages the control of motor speech articulators. In this paper, the main objective is to develop an efficient speech recognition module based on the Voice Input Voice Output Communication Aid (VIVOCA) architecture that can device a support aid to the people with DYSARTHRIA. Totally there are seven features extracted from each noise eliminated real time bilingual isolated word speech signal data uttered by a speaker both in Tamil and English languages. Vector Quantization based Genetic Algorithm codebook is created for the recognition modeling. Optimization of Hidden Markov Model (HMM) is done based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) method to improve the recognition accuracy compared to the conventional HMM and also experiment results of the proposed module shows 95% of accuracy. The proposed module will be very much useful for developing a speech recognition system that facilitates the patients and persons with special needs for communication. The proposed module is also evaluated for its complexity which will be therefore efficient for low consumption of energy.

Author Keywords: Vector Quantization (VQ) and Hidden Markov Model (HMM)

articleTitle: The socioeconomic determinants of use of Smartphones by the inhabitants of the metropolis of Casablanca
publicationTitle: 2018 Renewable Energies, Power Systems & Green Inclusive Economy (REPS-GIE)
abstract: In this paper, we are interested in the question of the adoption and use of Smartphones by the residents of the great metropolis of Casablanca. We conducted a survey of 1305 individuals. Two qualitative econometric models revealed that large differences are observed according to the socioeconomic status and living conditions of individuals.

articleTitle: AN ADVANCED COMPARATIVE STUDY OF SELF-ORGANIZATION PROTOCOLS IN WIRELESS SENSOR NETWORK
publicationTitle: 2018 Renewable Energies, Power Systems & Green Inclusive Economy (REPS-GIE)
abstract: Nowadays, wireless sensor networks (WSN) play a crucial role in various fields such as the army, health, the environment, and so on. These new sensors have limitations, which must be taken into consideration when deploying a WSN network, especially their strictly limited energy. Thus, in order to efficiently use the energy of these nodes to improve and increase the lifetime of the entire network, several self-organization algorithms have been proposed to create different network architectures based on required applications. In this article, we will study and examine the various WSN-based self-organization algorithms, highlighting their principles in order to compare them according to different metrics and on multiple requirements such as load balancing, energy efficiency, complexity of the algorithm ... etc. To perform this multi-criteria comparison, we will use the ROC (Rank Order Centroid) multicriteria analysis method, to make the decision when designing and implementing a new efficient and effective self-organization algorithm that will meet all metrics and to all criteria.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Control of PV System with the Series Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 Renewable Energies, Power Systems & Green Inclusive Economy (REPS-GIE)
abstract: The problem of Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) for photovoltaic (PV) arrays is addressed. The considered PV System includes a PV Generator (PVG) connected to DC Bus using a DC/DC Converter. Unlike standard PV systems, the used static converter is of the series resonant type (SRC). Indeed, this latter optimizes the power losses during the switching phases. The proposed output feedback control is a robust nonlinear controller, based on Nonlinear model of PV System, ought to be able to instantaneously determine the maximum power point (MPP) when solar irradiance and temperature are measurable. It is formally shown that the developed controller actually meets the MPPT objective. These theoretical results are confirmed by simulation.

articleTitle: Output Feedback Control for Wind Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 Renewable Energies, Power Systems & Green Inclusive Economy (REPS-GIE)
abstract: This paper deals with the control of wind energy systems with the doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) without recurring to any mechanical sensors. The control objective dressed here is twofold: maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and reactive power regulation in the DFIG. The designed controller is based on the nonlinear state-space representation of the controlled system, including a sliding mode controller and a high gain observer. The whole system enjoys a semi-global practical stability, proved using tools from the Lyapunov theory. These theoretical results are confirmed by simulations involving wide range variation of the wind speed.

articleTitle: Cultural Factors impacting the Global Energy Transition - A Review
publicationTitle: 2018 Renewable Energies, Power Systems & Green Inclusive Economy (REPS-GIE)
abstract: Energy transition from fossil fuels to renewable has been a case of debate in social, political, economic and environmental points of view owing to the long term impacts it has on populace and Governments. The energy transition requires infrastructural change for introduction, production and diffusion which takes decades to be developed. But the most important threat to the transition is the time and effort it takes to persuade the society for adaption. Many developed nations have shown improvement in the percentage of transition after a global movement took place in 2009 but still the larger part of the globe has not been able to adapt it. The paper compares various socio economic political and cultural factors affecting the transition in various countries both developing and developed. These perspectives are important for decision makers since they can adversely affect the intended benefits of any technology or at least slow down the transition.

articleTitle: Vulnerabilities of Industrial Control Systems Outside
publicationTitle: 2018 Renewable Energies, Power Systems & Green Inclusive Economy (REPS-GIE)
abstract: Discusses the vulnerability from the point of view of information security of modern control systems of technological processes. Such vulnerabilities inherent not only APCS for industrial facilities, but also in the life support systems of cities and the Internet of things (IoT). In particular, we consider the vulnerability of the typical converters of interfaces, such as the common parts of the automation systems. It is shown that many of them can be easily accessed from the outside even the untrained user. Proposed recommendations for improving the security of systems with such converters, and APCS at all.
